The virus "mutates" cells into mosquito eggs by warping the DNA? How does it do that? Does it work anomalously, or has the mechanism just not been investigated? Or has it been investigated?

I believe this is answered with this:

SCP-149 is a breed of mosquito which carries a strain of retrovirus (herein referred to as SCP-149-A)

A retrovirus edits DNA through a known biological process, complex but not anomalous.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This article seems to me to be somewhat logically unfeasible; that is, the description of the mechanism by which the "virus" works is so bare that it leaves me in want of some more details. The virus "mutates" cells into mosquito eggs by warping the DNA? How does it do that? Does it work anomalously, or has the mechanism just not been investigated? Or has it been investigated?

Not to mention, I would make the argument that this is decidedly un-keter by today's object class interpretation standards. Aside from a special contingency plan, they're basically locked in a box. The concept is really great, but the fact that the idea of mosquito larvae emerging from cysts inside of one's body makes most people (including me) extremely uncomfortable isn't enough to warrant an upvote. In my opinion, as entertaining a read as it was, the concept should be fleshed out a little bit more.

item.title: Overpowered | Suggest supernatural aspect
item.content:encoded:
The idea that the virus generates new mosquitoes within hours suggests more than simple biological modification. The human body can't work that fast, and nearly all arboviruses take weeks to show symptoms. Recommend changing incubation period to days/weeks. This implies greater believability (yes, I know this is an article about an imaginary mosquito/virus) and the chance for much larger dissemination, should an infected person be a traveler and return to their home country.

Still upvoted; just needs a few changes IMHO.

item.content:encoded:
The SCP-149-A is only able to survive in the saliva of SCP-149.

That would mean it wouldn't survive in blood.

As a response to this, O5 command has created Protocol-42-Charlie, to be used whenever SCP-149 escapes confinement.

Should be IF unless there are capabilities not listed.

And on THAT note, it's a safely contained bug. It's not Keter. Yes, it could destroy all of mankind (maybe all the warmblooded life - don't know if it can infect non-human) but it's CONTAINED and doesn't seem to require more extensive procedures then an entomologist would normally have. Advise downgrading to Euclid.

Then I advise killing it with a hammer. GOD I hate this thing!

Upvoting.
